front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name is from Ayat 21.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah was revealed late in the 10th or early in the 11th year of Prophethood. The timing is based on the visit of the Jinn, as mentioned in Ayats 29-32, which occurred when the Prophet returned to Makkah from Ta'if.

front_matter.label: Historical Background
front_matter.text:
The tenth year of the Prophethood was marked by intense persecution for the Holy Prophet, as the Quraish and allied tribes enforced a three-year boycott against the Bani Hashim and Muslims, leaving them besieged and deprived of supplies. Abu Lahab actively encouraged merchants to inflate prices, worsening their hardship.
After the siege ended, both Abu Talib, the Prophet's protective uncle, and Khadijah, his supportive wife, died within weeks, making it a year of sorrow and grief. The Prophet then faced increased hostility in Makkah, including public humiliation. Seeking new opportunities, he traveled on foot to Ta'if to invite its leaders to Islam but was rejected and assaulted. Injured and exhausted, he prayed for strength rather than vengeance.
Returning to Makkah, he worried about further opposition, but found hope when a group of jinn heard him recite the Quran, believed, and began sharing his message.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text: Its main purpose is to warn disbelievers about their misconceptions—rejecting accountability, denying the Prophet's mission, dismissing the Quran as God's word, and refusing belief in life after death. It is a pair of the previous Surah. The previous Surah told us to leave arrogance. Here too the contrast between arrogance and humility continues. This is the last of the Ha Mim Surahs.

sections.title: 1-6 ALLAH CREATED THE HEAVENS, EARTH AND ALL THAT LIES BETWEEN THEM TO MANIFEST THE TRUTH AND THOSE DEITIES TO WHOM MUSHRIKIN INVOKE ARE NOT EVEN AWARE THAT THEY ARE BEING INVOKED

translation.text: Ha'. Mim.
The revelation of this Book is from Allah, the Most Mighty, the Most Wise.
We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in Truth and for an appointed term. But those who disbelieve have turned away from what they were warned against.

commentary.text: Ayat 1, 2 and 3 are the same as the last Surah. That this is a world with a purpose for a limited period. Warning about the DoJ is given.

translation.text: Who could be more wrong than a person who calls on those other than God, those who will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection, those who are unaware of his prayers,

commentary.text: Shirk is being refuted. No one is more misguided than those who invoke idols (anyone else) besides Allah SWT, asking them for things that they cannot give. They (the idols) are unaware of what he asks, because they can neither hear, see, or act. Like sending an email to the wrong address and expecting a reply.

Usually, this shirk is divided into three categories: 
(1) Lifeless and inanimate creation. 
(2) The pious men who have passed away. 
(3) The wicked men who had themselves gone astray, and who misled others and passed away.

“Those who will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection…” means that during the world or their lifetime they will get no answer to their supplications and prayers from their deities, but when Resurrection will have taken place, the deities will turn hostile to their worshipers themselves, as becomes explicit from the following Ayat.

translation.text: Those who, when all mankind is gathered, will become his enemies and disown his worship?

commentary.text: Shirk is being refuted repeatedly. In this world duas or prayers to false gods will go unanswered and in the other world the false gods will disown them.
FYI – Righteous and pious people would never want to be worshipped. All Prophets including Jesus (PBUH) called people to Tauhid.

sections.title: 7-10 AL-QURAN IS THE WORD OF ALLAH, NOT THE PROPHET AND PROPHET IS BUT A PLAIN WARNER

translation.text: Do they claim that the Messenger himself has fabricated it? (If so), tell them: “If I have fabricated it, then you have no power to protect me from Allah's chastisement. He knows well the idle talk in which you indulge. He suffices as a witness between me and you. He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Say, ‘Have you thought: what if this Quran really is from God and you reject it? What if one of the Children of Israel testifies to its similarity [to earlier scripture] and believes in it, and yet you are too proud to [do the same]? God certainly does not guide evildoers.’

sections.title: 11-14 AL-QURAN CONFORMS THE REVELATION OF TORAH GIVEN TO PROPHET MUSA

translation.text: Yet the scripture of Moses was revealed before it as a guide and a mercy, and this is a scripture confirming it in the Arabic language to warn those who do evil and bring good news for those who do good.

commentary.text: The Quran confirms the Torah, and the Torah confirms the Quran as divine scriptures.

translation.text: Surely those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast—there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.

commentary.text: IMAN + STEADFASTNESS = SUCCESS.
Once you say you believe then remain steadfast on it. Remain firm. For such people Allah SWT promises Paradise.

sections.title: 15-20 THOSE WHO TREAT THEIR PARENTS WITH KINDNESS SHALL BE REWARDED AND THOSE WHO REBUKE THEIR PARENTS SHALL BE PUNISHED

translation.text: We have commanded man to be good to his parents: his mother struggled to carry him and struggled to give birth to him– his bearing and weaning took a full thirty months. When he has grown to manhood and reached the age of forty he [may] say, ‘Lord, help me to be truly

commentary.text: grateful for Your favours to me and to my parents; help me to do good work that pleases You; make my offspring good. I turn to You; I am one of those who devote themselves to You.’
In Ayat 14, after mentioning His Oneness, worship Him with sincerity, and remain upright in obeying Him, Allah follows that by giving instructions regarding the parents.

In this Ayat Allah SWT commands us to be good to one’s parents i.e., both the mother and the father, however the mother’s rights are greater on the grounds that she undergoes greater hardships for the sake of the children.

A Hadith, to the effect that a person asked the Prophet (PBUH): Who has got a greater right to my service? The Prophet replied (PBUH): Your mother. He asked: Who after her? He replied: Your mother. He asked: Who after her? He replied: Your mother. He asked: Who after her? He replied: Your father.

This Hadith precisely explains this Ayat, for here also Allah SWT has mentioned the triple right of the mother: (1) His mother bore him with hardship. (2) She gave him birth with hardship. (3) His bearing and his weaning took thirty months. 

A legal point derived from this Ayat and in Surah Luqman Ayat 14 and Surah Al- Baqarah Ayat 223) which was pointed out by Ali and Ibn Abbas in a law case and made Uthman change his decision.

The story goes that during the caliphate of Uthman, a person married a woman from the Juhainah tribe, and just six months after the marriage she gave birth to a healthy and sound child. The man took the case before Uthman, who declared the woman to be an adulteress and ordered that she be stoned to death. On hearing this Ali immediately came to Uthman and asked: What sort of a decision have you given? He replied: She has given birth to a sound child six months after marriage. Is it not a clear proof of her being an adulteress? Ali did not agree and recited the three above mentioned Ayats in their sequence.

In Surah Al-Baqarah Allah says: The mothers shall suckle their children for two whole years, if the fathers desire the suckling to be completed. In Surah Luqman it is said: And his weaning took two years, and in Surah Al-Ahqaf: his bearing and his weaning took thirty months.

Now, if two years of suckling are taken away from 30 months, six months of bearing remain. This shows that the minimum period of pregnancy in which a sound child can be born is six months. Therefore, the woman who has given birth to a child six months after the marriage cannot be declared an adulteress. On hearing this reasoning of Ali, Uthman admitted that he had not considered that thing at all. Then he recalled the woman and changed his decision.

“And reaches forty years.”., meaning, his complete intellect, understanding, and patience reach the level of maturity. It has also been said that usually one will not change his ways once he reaches the age of forty.

Our parents blessing has been transferred to us including good family, money, prestige, good education etc. So be grateful to your parents.

commentary.text: So, making parents happy is making Allah SWT happy.
Hadith: Story about a man who killed a man. To repent he was told to do ahsaan to his parents.
People who are good to their parents then Allah SWT accepts their good deeds in this life.

There is pride in the child.
Allah SWT has prohibited disrespect towards the parents and especially towards the mother.

translation.text: It is against such that Allah's sentence (of punishment) has become due. They will join the communities of humans and jinn that have preceded them. Verily all of them will court utter loss.
Each ˹of the two groups˺ will be ranked according to what they have done so He may fully reward all. And none will be wronged.

commentary.text: A person will have the rank according to his deeds i.e. not inherited. Compensated fully by Allah SWT. We see the consequences of our deeds in this life as well for example if we are bad to our parents usually our children are bad to us.

So Today you will be rewarded with the torment of disgrace for your arrogance throughout the land with no right, and for your rebelliousness.”

commentary.text: If a person wants the world he will be given (a portion of the world) but then will get nothing in the Hereafter.
The companions of the Prophet (PBUH) feared worldly blessings because they feared they would not get anything in the Hereafter.
Traits Allah SWT does not like and lead to failure. (i) WORLDLY OBSESSION AND (ii) ARROGANCE AND (iii) BEING RUDE OR DISRESPECTING YOUR PARENTS.

commentary.text: Allah SWT send Prophet Hud, (PBUH) to the nation of Ad to warn them.  Ad who inhabited Al-Ahqaf.
Ahqaf means a sand dune.  They dwelt among sand (hills) and overlooked the sea. But they rejected! And in their arrogance asked when will the punishment you speak of come?
Name of Surah.
Trait of mocking and denying after knowledge.

translation.text: When they saw a cloud approaching their valley, they said, ‘This cloud will give us rain!’ ‘No indeed! It is what you wanted to hasten: a storm-wind bearing a painful punishment.

commentary.text:
Then, when they saw dense clouds approaching their valleys, meaning, when they saw the punishment coming towards them, they thought the clouds were full of rain. That made them happy and joyful, because they had a drought and needed rain. But infact this was a painful torment!
For eight days and seven nights this violent wind did not stop. Ripping everything out and killing everyone.

sections.title: 27-28 NO DEITY CAN SAVE PEOPLE FROM THE WRATH OF ALLAH

translation.text: Why then did those ˹idols˺ they took as gods—hoping to get closer ˹to Him˺—not come to their aid? Instead, they failed them. That is ˹the result of˺ their lies and their fabrications.

commentary.text: Initially people put faith in those idols/people with the idea that they would attain nearness to Allah SWT through them, but then gradually they made them their gods. They started invoking them for help; believing that they have the powers to change destinies and could answer their prayers and remove their hardships.
Allah SWT sent His revelations through His Messengers over and over again in different ways to bring them to the right path, but they persisted in the worship of their idols/gods.

Now consider this: When the torment of Allah SWT visited these polytheists because of their deviation, where had their redressers of grievances and removers of hardships disappeared? Why didn’t they come to their rescue at the time of affliction?
Thus far we see in this Surah traits of those who are grateful and humble vs those who are arrogant and full of pride.

sections.title: 29-34 A GROUP OF JINNS EMBRACED ISLAM AFTER HEARING AL-QURAN AND BECAME THE PREACHERS TO THEIR FOLK

translation.text: Remember, O Prophet,˺ when We sent a group of jinn your way to listen to the Quran. Then, upon hearing it, they said ˹to one another˺, “Listen quietly!” Then when it was over, they returned to their fellow jinn as warners.

commentary.text: This incident occurred towards the end of the Makkan era with the boycott of Banu Hashim. The year of sorrow because the Prophet (PBUH) lost his wife and uncle. The Prophet (PBUH) had no protection and was chased out of the city but then later went back to Makkah. During the Prophet’s (PBUH) return journey from Taif to Makkah he is feeling very sad. On the way, when he halted at Nakhlah, and the Prophet (PBUH) took comfort by salah and reciting the Quran a group of the jinns happened to pass by and stopped to listen to him. Allah SWT informed the Prophet (PBUH) afterwards by revelation that they had come and listened to the Quranic recitation.
Allah SWT created the circumstances that the two will meet. This happens in life as well. So there is no such thing as coincidence or by chance of meeting someone.
Lesson: Jinn heard accepted immediately and began conveying. Never know who will accept so just give dawa.

translation.text: They said: “Our people, We have heard a Scripture revealed after Moses, verifying the Scriptures revealed before it; it guides to the Truth and to the Straight Way.

commentary.text: This shows that these jinns had already had faith in the Prophet Musa (PBUH) and in the divine Books. After hearing the Quran, they felt that it gave the same teachings as the former Prophets had been preaching. Therefore, they believed in this Book forthwith and in the Prophet (PBUH) who had brought it.

translation.text: Our people, respond to the one who calls you to God. Believe in Him: He will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful torment.’

front_matter.label: Bismillah
front_matter.text: سۡمِ اللهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِ

front_matter.label: JUZ
front_matter.text: JUZ 26

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah derives its name from Ayat 2. Besides this name the Surah has another well-known name "al-Qital" from Ayat 20.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The contents of this Surah testify that it was sent down after the hijrah at Madinah at the time when the command for fighting had been given, although active fighting had not yet been undertaken. It is a pair with Surah Bakarah.

front_matter.label: Historical Background
front_matter.text:
Life for Muslims at the time this Surah was revealed was extremely difficult. In Makkah and across Arabia, believers faced relentless persecution. Even after emigrating to Madinah, the Quraish refused to leave them in peace. The small community of Muslims in Madinah was surrounded by enemies, intent on eradicating them completely.
Daily existence in Madinah was marked by fear and deprivation. Many emigrants remained homeless, struggling to find stability. Food was scarce, and basic supplies were hard to come by. The economic boycott imposed by the Quraish cut off food and supplies from Madinah. Some families went days with little to eat, relying on whatever support their fellow Muslims could muster. The constant threat of attack heightened anxiety, and the atmosphere was tense.
At this crucial moment, the Muslims had two choices. (i) They could surrender to the forces of ignorance, abandoning their mission and even their private practice of faith. (ii) Or they could risk everything and wage war to determine whether Islam would endure in Arabia or be erased by the dominant pagan traditions. Allah SWT guided the believers to choose the path of determination and courage and permitted them to fight.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its theme is to prepare the believers for war and to give them preliminary instructions in this regard. That is why it has also been entitled al-Qital.  The Surah advises believers on conduct in war, promises rewards for their sacrifices, and references the expulsion of Muhammad from Makkah as a crucial event.
Surah Muhammad addresses disbelievers and hypocrites, but its primary moral exposure is of hypocrisy within the Muslim community, not open disbelief.
Disbelievers are mentioned clearly at the start. They openly reject faith, block people from Allah SWT’s path, and oppose the Messenger(PBUH). Their stance is external and obvious.
Hypocrites are the deeper problem the Surah keeps circling back to. They claim belief, sit among Muslims, but recoil from sacrifice, fear struggle, sow corruption, sever ties, and collapse morally when tested.
Surah Muhammad is highly patterned and the Surah repeatedly works in paired movements, not isolated Ayats. There are are key structural and thematic patterns people usually miss.
Disbeliever (kāfir)
A disbeliever openly rejects faith. There is no pretense.
Does not claim belief in Allah SWT or the Messenger (PBUH)
Is clear and consistent about rejection
Is judged on open disbelief, not deception
The problem here is denial, not dishonesty.
Hypocrite (munāfiq)
A hypocrite claims belief outwardly but rejects it inwardly.
Publicly says “I believe”
Privately disbelieves, undermines, or works against Islam
Uses faith as cover for self-interest, fear, or power
This is why hypocrisy is treated as more dangerous. It corrodes from the inside.
Why the hypocrite is worse
The disbeliever stands outside the faith.
The hypocrite stands inside and sabotages it.
Disbelief is a position; hypocrisy is a betrayal.
The Qur’an repeatedly states that hypocrites will be in a lower depth of Hell because their crime is not just rejection, but deception plus harm.

sections.title: 1-3 ALLAH VOID THE DEEDS OF THE DISBELIEVERS

translation.text: Allah has caused the works of those who disbelieve and hinder people from the way of Allah to go to waste.

commentary.text: Meaning, Allah SWT renders their deeds useless and futile, and He denies them any rewards or blessings for them.

Also see Surah 25 Ayat 23
“And We will approach what they have done of deeds and make them as dispersed dust.”

translation.text: But those who believe and work deeds of righteousness, and believe in the (Revelation) sent down to Muhammad - for it is the Truth from their Lord,- He will remove from them their ills and improve their condition.

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer. Their outcome in relation to their deeds and striving.
IMAN + RIGHTEOUS DEEDS + IMAN IN THE PROPHET (PBUH) = SUCCESS/PARADISE.
After the trials in Mecca the companions now have become pure gold. Their character is praiseworthy all by Allah SWT mercy and guidance.

sections.title: 4-6 IN CASE OF WAR THOROUGHLY SUBDUE THE UNBELIEVERS BEFORE TAKING PRISONERS OF WAR

translation.text: When you meet the disbelievers in battle, strike them in the neck, and once they are defeated, bind any captives firmly––later you can release them by grace or by ransom––until the toils of war have ended. That [is the way]. God could have defeated them Himself if He had willed, but His purpose is to test some of you by means of others. He will not let the deeds of those who are killed for His cause come to nothing;

commentary.text:
This is an Ayat that people often misinterpret and find hard to understand. In this Surah many Ayats are related to battel that are specific to the Prophet (PBUH) so understand the context. 
It appears that this Ayah was revealed after the battle of Badr. At that time, Allah SWT reproached the believers for sparing many of the enemy's soldiers and holding too many captives for ransom.
Background: In Mecca for 13 years the Muslims were forbidden to fight with the strategy of forgiveness and patience but now the command to fight is clear.

Also see (8:67-68)
It is not for a Prophet to have captives of war until he had made a great slaughter (among the enemies) in the land. You desire the commodities of this world, but Allah desires (for you) the Hereafter. Allah is Mighty and Wise. Were it not for a prior decree from Allah, a severe torment would have touched you for what you took.

The etiquette of war is given here. The command to fight is explicit. (i) First command is to strike the neck of the enemy meaning destroy them decisively. Allah SWT is being very explicit and graphic here. Do not negotiate or let the enemy retreat.  (ii) Once the enemy has been totally subjugated only then only can you take captives, (iii) then you have the choice of releasing them (captives) with grace or random. But always treat captives very well.
The purpose of war in Islam is not war booty or property rather it is the propagation of Islam.

So, the rule is that first you must completely destroy the enemy. Here it is imperative to understand the difference between battle and war. Only when the war is won (not battel) and there is no resistance that this rule of captives /prisoners is allowed. Once a Revolution has been firmly established only then. Logic is that in Battel of Badr when you released the prisoners they then could go back and begin resistance all over again.

“God could have defeated them Himself if He had willed, but His purpose is to test some of you by means of others”,,..” means Allah SWT has ordered Jihad and fighting against the enemies in order to test you.
Allah SWT also expresses His wisdom by the legislation of Jihad in the following two Surahs, Al `Imran and At-Tawbah, in which He says:

(3:142)
Or did you think that you would enter the Paradise before Allah had made evident those of you who fight in His cause and made evident those who are steadfast. 
(9:14-15)
Fight them; Allah will then punish them by your hands, disgrace them, grant you victory over them, satisfy the breasts of a believing people, and remove the fury of their (the believers') hearts. Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills; Allah is Knowing and Wise.

Merit of the Martyrs
Since it is customary during wars that many of the believers die, Allah SWT says: He would not let their good deeds go to waste but would rather multiply and increase them. Some of them will continue being rewarded for their good deeds for the entire length of their stay in Al-Barzakh.

sections.title: 7-11 IF YOU HELP THE CAUSE OF ALLAH, ALLAH WILL HELP AND PROTECT YOU

translation.text: You who believe! If you help God, He will help you and make you stand firm.

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer.
If you help Allah SWT that is, if you participate in the work of raising Allah’s Word with your life and wealth. But this has a deeper meaning too. Also see Surah Al-Imran Ayat 52.
Conditions need to strive for Allah SWT’s deen (i) Do this for Allah SWT only (ii) Don’t change or alter religion (iii) Stive with all your effort.
This is an act where Allah SWT’s help is guaranteed. Additionally, Tawfiq and steadfastness in religion is given by Allah SWT.
May Allah SWT make me of those who strive for Allah SWT. Ameen.

translation.text: As for the disbelievers, may they be doomed and may He render their deeds void.

commentary.text: For those who deny there is misery in this world and the next. And all deeds are void. Meaning complete and utter destruction.
May Allah SWT protect us from us a fate. Ameen.

translation.text: That is because they detest what Allah has revealed, so He has rendered their deeds void.

arabic_lines: ذَٰلِكَ   بِأَنَّ   ٱللَّهَ   مَوْلَى   ٱلَّذِينَ   آمَنُوا   وَأَنَّ   ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ   لَا   مَوْلَىٰ   لَهُمْ

translation.text: That is because Allah is the Protector of the believers whereas the unbelievers have none to protect them.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is always the protector or Mula of all believers. (Beautiful).

sections.title: 12-14 BELIEVERS DO NOT FOLLOW THEIR OWN DESIRES

translation.text: Allah shall admit those who believe and do righteous works to the Gardens beneath which rivers flow. As for the unbelievers, they enjoy the pleasures of this transient life and eat as cattle eat. The Fire shall be their resort.

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer.
IMAN + RIGHTEOUS DEEDS = SUCCESS

Those who deny are compared to living their lives like animals. They are like animals so just satisfy their base instincts eat, poop etc., in this life just blindly pursing their desires while caring or preparing nothing for the next life. (Not a pretty comparision).
Humans unlike animals have a higher purpose and greater goal i.e. prepare of the afterlife by worshipping Allah.

translation.text: Can those who follow clear proof from their Lord be compared to those whose foul deeds are made to seem alluring to them, those who follow their own desires?

commentary.text: Also see Surah 59 Ayat 20
Not equal are the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise. The People of Paradise will be the successful ones.
Comparison between a believer and non-believer.
Now a comparison between a believer and a non-believer (one who follows their desires) is given. Thus, the consequences for each will be different as well.

sections.title: 15 PARABLE OF PARADISE AND HELL

translation.text: Here is a picture of the Garden promised to the pious: rivers of water forever pure, rivers of milk forever fresh, rivers of wine, a delight for those who drink, rivers of honey clarified and pure, [all] flow in it; there they will find fruit of every kind; and they will find forgiveness from their Lord. How can this be compared to the fate of those stuck in the Fire, given boiling water to drink that tears their bowels?

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer.
Description of Paradise Compared to Hell

Hadith: When you ask Allah SWT, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, because it is the central and highest part of the Paradise, and from it gush the rivers of the Paradise and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.

sections.title: 16-19 HYPOCRITES ARE THOSE ON WHOSE HEART ALLAH HAS SET A SEAL

translation.text: Some of these people listen to you [Prophet], but, once they leave your presence, they sneer at those who have been given knowledge, saying, ‘What was that he just said?’ These are the ones whose hearts God has sealed, those who follow their own desires.

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer.

This is an early Madian Surah, and this is when hypocrisy began. This Ayat is concerning those disbelievers and hypocrites who were followers of the former Books and sat in the assemblies of the Prophet (PBUH) listening to his sermons, or the Ayats of the Quran. But since in their hearts they were averse to the themes presented, they would understand nothing despite their listening. Therefore, when they came out, they would ask the Muslims: What was he saying just now?

Such are the men whose hearts Allah SWT has sealed. They were the slaves of their lusts, and the teachings that the Prophet (PBUH) fell against their lusts. Therefore, if ever they sat in the assemblies of the Prophet (PBUH) and listened to him, they would understand nothing.

translation.text: God has increased the guidance of those who follow the right path and given them their awareness [of Him].

commentary.text: Those who seek guidance, Allah SWT facilitates it for them; He guides them to it, makes them firm on it, and gives them more of it.

That is, the same revelations about which the disbelievers and hypocrites ask: What was the Prophet (PBUH) saying just now? become a cause of further guidance for the rightly guided people, and from the same assembly from which these unfortunate people rise without gaining anything, the fortunate ones return with a new treasure of knowledge and insight. Allah SWT grants them the grace to develop in themselves a piety (taqwa).

sections.title: 20-28 PROMISE OF OBEDIENCE (ISLAM) AND GOOD TALK WHICH IS NOT FOLLOWED BY ACTION IS CURSED BY ALLAH

translation.text: The believers used to say: “Why is a surah (that would ordain fighting) not revealed?” But when a definitive surah was revealed wherein fighting was mentioned, you saw that those in whose hearts there was a sickness looked at you as though they were about to faint at the approach of death. Pity on them!

commentary.text: Also name of Surah
Comparison between a sincere believer and non-believer (hypocrite)

Due to persecution, many Muslims were eager for divine permission to fight their oppressors, asking impatiently why they could not take action. Then when a definitive Surah was revealed and when fighting was finally commanded, the distinction between true believers and hypocrites became clear—despite outwardly practicing faith, the hypocrites hesitated to make sacrifices. Thus, those who joined Islam insincerely valued their own safety and possessions above faith and were unwilling to risk them.
The difference between a sincere believer and non-believer (hypocrite) is our reaction to Allah SWT’s commands. A believer wants to obey every command while a hypocrite disobeys or finds excuses.

translation.text: to obey and speak rightly. Then when fighting was ordained, it surely would have been better for them if they were true to Allah.

commentary.text: The command to fight was final so it would have been better for them to obey, speak good words and fulfill their promise to Allah SWT. A promise to fight however they retreated.

translation.text: Now if you ˹hypocrites˺ turn away, perhaps you would then spread corruption throughout the land and sever your ˹ties of˺ kinship!

commentary.text: This Ayat warns that if people refuse to sincerely support and sacrifice for Islam, the inevitable result is a return to corruption, injustice, and mutual violence, just as in the age of ignorance. It also exposes moral hypocrisy: when faith is claimed without willingness to uphold its demands, any power granted will only produce tyranny and bloodshed, even against one’s own kin.
The Ayat firmly condemns the severing of family ties, a principle reinforced repeatedly in the Quran, and establishes kindness to relatives as a major virtue.
Struggles and test from Allah SWT keep us humble and teach us how to lead.

translation.text: This, because they said to those who are averse to the faith that Allah has revealed: “In some matters we shall obey you.” Allah has full knowledge of their secret parleys.

commentary.text: Hypocrites are revealed
Despite professing the faith and being counted among the Muslims, they went on conspiring secretly with the enemies of Islam and even pledged to support them in certain matters.

translation.text: Then how ˹horrible˺ will it be when the angels take their souls, beating their faces and backs!

commentary.text: That is, how their situation will be when the angels come to take their lives, and their souls cling to their bodies, causing the angels to extract them by force, harshness, and beating.

translation.text: This is because they follow whatever displeases Allah and hate whatever pleases Him, so He has rendered their deeds void.

sections.title: 29-34 ALLAH PUT THE BELIEVERS TO TEST IN ORDER TO KNOW THE VALIANT AND THE RESOLUTE

translation.text: We will certainly test you ˹believers˺ until We prove those of you who ˹truly˺ struggle ˹in Allah’s cause˺ and remain steadfast, and reveal how you conduct yourselves.

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer.

Allah SWT will certainly test the believers with commands and prohibitions. It is not just about trials in life but also how we respond to divine instructions. This is how Allah SWT distinguishes between the Mujaheddin (those who do strive/do jihad in Allah SWT’s way) from those (the hypocrites) who are making excuses.
These tests are not for Allah SWT has He already knows rather for believers to manifest their true state of heart and actions.
Lesson: We will all be tested so get ready!

translation.text: Indeed, those who disbelieve, hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and defy the Messenger after ˹true˺ guidance has become clear to them; they will not harm Allah in the least, but He will render their deeds void.

commentary.text: Three sins/crimes are mentioned here:
Kufur or denial
Stopping/hindering people from Allah’s Way
Opposing the Messenger (PBUH) after knowledge has come to them.

This has two meanings: 
(1) That Allah will render vain and fruitless all those works which they had performed as good works, and they will get no reward whatever for them in the Hereafter. 

(2) That all the devices that they are adopting to obstruct the way of Allah and His Messenger’s (peace be upon him) religion will prove ineffective and fruitless.

translation.text: Believers, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not cause your works to be nullified.

commentary.text: Comparison between a believer and non-believer.

In other words, the deeds being beneficial and yielding of good results depends wholly on one’s obedience to Allah and His Messenger. After one has turned away from obedience, no deed remains a good deed so that one may deserve any reward for it.

translation.text: Surely those who disbelieve, hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and then die as disbelievers; Allah will never forgive them.

commentary.text: Those who (i) reject faith and turn away and (ii) then hinder others in the way of Allah and (iii) then die in this state – Allah SWT will never forgive them. This conclusion is both direct and severe.
Also see Surah Nisa Ayat 48
Verily, Allah does not forgive joining partners with Him in worship, but He forgives except that to whom He wills.
Lesson: Shirk and apostasy are sins that are unforgivable. Be mindful of your own faith and how you instruct others.
Never obstruct people from Allah SWT’s way.

sections.title: 35-36 IN THE CASE OF WAR ALLAH IS ON THE SIDE OF THE BELIEVERS

translation.text: So do not falter or cry for peace, for you will have the upper hand and Allah is with you. And He will never let your deeds go to waste.

commentary.text: Muslims in Madina were not safe but Allah SWT says don’t be afraid.

All these Ayats teach us that do not be afraid or weak concerning the enemies and beg for peace or compromise to end the fighting between you and the disbelievers while you are in a position of power/superiority both in numbers and preparations.
Here it is important to contextualize and not generalize.
Allah will never invalidate your deeds, nullify them, or deprive you of them, but rather He will give you your rewards complete, without any reduction.

translation.text: The life of this world is only a game, a pastime, but if you believe and are mindful of God, He will recompense you. He does not ask you to give up [all] your possessions–

commentary.text:
Showing the Triviality of the Worldly Life and encouraging Spending
Expressing the insignificance and worthlessness of the worldly life, Allah SWT says, this worldly life is only amusement and diversion. And if you believe and have Taqwa of Allah, He will grant you your rewards, and will not ask from you (to sacrifice all) your possessions.
IMAN + PIETY = SUCCESS
LESSON: LIFE FULL OF AMUSEMENT IS A WASTED LIFE.

sections.title: 37-38 DO NOT BE NIGGARDLY IF YOU ARE ASKED TO GIVE IN THE CAUSE OF ALLAH

translation.text: If He were to ask you for your possessions and press you (in that regard), you would have grown niggardly, and Allah would have brought your failings to light.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is in no need of you. He only ordained giving charity from your wealth so that you would help your needy brothers. The benefit of that would then come back to you, as well as the rewards.

translation.text: Here you are, being invited to donate ˹a little˺ in the cause of Allah. Still some of you withhold. And whoever does so, it is only to their own loss. For Allah is the Self-Sufficient, whereas you stand in need ˹of Him˺. If you ˹still˺ turn away, He will replace you with another people. And they will not be like you.

commentary.text: This is an invitation from Allah SWT to earn reward, yet some are stingy. Here stinginess refers to not spending in the way or cause of Allah SWT yet fulfilling one’s own desires.  Their stinginess reduces rewards and backfires on them because Allah SWT sends trials their way. Allah SWT is without need and we are always in need of Allah SWT.
Powerful ending: If we don’t listen and obey then Allah SWT will replace us. He does not need us rather we need Him so understand your position in life.

front_matter.label: Bismillah
front_matter.text: سۡمِ اللهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِ

front_matter.label: JUZ
front_matter.text: JUZ 26

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: It is from Ayat 1. This is not only a name of the Surah but also its subject matter, for it deals with the great victory that Allah SWT granted to the Holy Prophet and the Muslims in the form of the Truce of Hudaibiyah.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Revealed at a time when the Holy Prophet was on his return journey to Madinah after concluding the Truce of Hudaibiyah with the disbelievers of Makkah.

front_matter.label: Historical Background
front_matter.text:
The Messenger of Allah SWT saw in a dream that he and his Companions were performing ʿumrah in Makkah. Understanding this as divine guidance, he announced the journey despite the danger posed by the Quraysh, who had barred Muslims from the Kaʿbah for years and had recently attempted to destroy Madinah during the Battle of the Trench. Around 1,400 unarmed Companions set out in the sacred month of Dhul-Qaʿdah, carrying sacrificial animals to signal peaceful intent.
The Quraysh, fearing loss of authority yet bound by Arabian norms that forbade fighting during sacred months, chose to block the Muslims. When informed that the Quraysh planned interception, the Prophet (PBUH) altered the route and camped at Ḥudaybiyyah, just outside Makkah. Envoys were exchanged. Leaders from Banu Khuzaʿah and later ʿUrwah ibn Masʿud confirmed that the Muslims intended only pilgrimage.
Despite this, the Quraysh repeatedly attempted to provoke violence through surprise attacks, all of which were met with restraint and forgiveness. When ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan was sent as an envoy and rumors spread that he had been killed, the Companions pledged unwavering loyalty under a tree in the Pledge of Riḍwān, ready to fight if necessary.
Negotiations eventually produced the Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah: a ten-year truce, postponement of ʿumrah until the following year, return of Qurayshi fugitives (but not vice versa), and freedom for tribes to ally with either side. Though the terms appeared humiliating, the Prophet (PBUH) accepted them. The emotional low point came when Abu Jandal, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr’s imprisoned son, escaped and was returned per the treaty, deeply distressing the Muslims.
As the Muslims returned to Madinah disheartened, revelation declared the treaty a “clear victory.”
The Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah completely shifted the balance of power in favor of the Muslims. By signing it, the Quraysh implicitly accepted the Islamic state as a legitimate political entity, which removed the stigma and hostility surrounding Islam. The ten-year peace created safe conditions for preaching, so Islam spread faster in two years than it had in nearly two decades. With no external war pressure, the Prophet (PBUH) strengthened Islamic law and social order in Madinah. When the Quraysh later violated the treaty, the Muslims marched into Makkah with 10,000 followers, not as vulnerable pilgrims but as a dominant force.
Even the clause that seemed most humiliating, returning Qurayshi fugitives, ultimately failed and turned against the Quraysh themselves, proving the treaty to be a decisive victory in disguise. The clause failed because enforcing it created an uncontrollable Muslim force outside Madinah that crippled Quraysh trade, forcing Quraysh themselves to abolish the condition.
The Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah was a peace agreement made in 6 AH between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh of Makkah. In short:
A 10-year truce was declared between both sides.
Muslims would return without performing ʿumrah that year but could come back the next year for a limited pilgrimage.
Any Makkan who fled to the Muslims would be returned, but anyone leaving the Muslims would not be returned.
Arab tribes were free to ally with either side.

sections.title: 1-10 ALLAH GRANTED THE MUSLIMS A MANIFEST VICTORY THROUGH THE TREATY OF HUDEYBIYAH AND SWEARING ALLEGIANCE TO THE PROPHET IS CONSIDERED SWEARING ALLEGIANCE TO ALLAH

translation.text: Indeed, We have granted you a clear triumph ˹O Prophet˺

commentary.text:
The Reason behind revealing Surat Al-Fath
This Surah was revealed after the Messenger of Allah returned from the area of Al-Hudaybiyyah, during the month of Dhul-Qadah, in the sixth year of Hijrah. This is when the idolators prevented him from reaching Al-Masjid Al-Haram to perform the Umrah he intended. A peace treaty was concluded stipulating that the Messenger (PBUH) would go back to Madina this year only to return for Umrah the following year. The Messenger agreed. However, some of the Companions disliked these terms, including Umar bin Al-Khattab.

Allah SWT declared the Al-Hudaybiyyah peace treaty a manifest victory. The Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah completely shifted the balance of power in favor of the Muslims. By signing it, the Quraysh implicitly accepted the Islamic state as a legitimate political entity, which removed the stigma and hostility surrounding Islam. The ten-year peace created safe conditions for preaching, so Islam spread faster in two years than it had in nearly two decades. With no external war pressure, the Prophet (PBUH) strengthened Islamic law and social order in Madinah. When the Quraysh later violated the treaty, the Muslims marched into Makkah with 10,000 followers, not as vulnerable pilgrims but as a dominant force.

Lesson: What seemed like a disgrace/humiliation was a gateway to successes. At times via apparent loss Allah SWT brings us much KHAIR/GOOD. Trust Allah SWT in all situations and never say anything negative about Him.

translation.text: So He may admit believing men and women into Gardens under which rivers flow—to stay there forever—and absolve them of their sins. And that is a supreme achievement in the sight of Allah.

commentary.text: Allah SWT explains the ultimate purpose behind the events of Ḥudaybiyyah: it was to admit believing men and believing women into Paradise, where they will live forever, and to erase their sins completely. Women are mentioned explicitly here to remove any doubt that reward is only for men. Although they did not travel to Ḥudaybiyyah, believing women shared fully in the struggle by encouraging their families, safeguarding homes and children, maintaining morale, and trusting Allah SWT without panic or fear. Their moral courage and sacrifice made them equal partners in reward.

Allah SWT also promises not merely forgiveness, but total purification: every trace of human weakness or mistake is removed before entry into Paradise, so believers enter without shame, regret, or moral residue. This, Allah declares, is the supreme victory not territory, not treaties, but eternal success with a clean record.
In short: Ḥudaybiyyah looked like loss, but its real reward was Paradise, shared equally by faithful men and women.
Lesson: Every test is a pathway to Paradise (depending on how you deal with it).

translation.text: Also ˹so that˺ He may punish hypocrite men and women and polytheistic men and women, who harbour evil thoughts of Allah. May ill-fate befall them! Allah is displeased with them. He has condemned them and prepared for them Hell. What an evil destination!

commentary.text: The hypocrites (both male and female) living in the suburbs of Al-Madinah were thinking, as has been stated in Ayat 12, below, that the Prophet (PBUH) and his companions would not return alive from that journey. As for the polytheists of Makkah (both male and female) and their pagan companions, they were thinking that they had successfully defeated the Prophet (PBUH) and his companions by preventing them from performing Umrah.

These groups question the wisdom of Allah SWT decisions and assumed bad thoughts about Allah SWT that He has abandoned His Prophet (PBUH). Allah SWT is displeased with such people! Severe punishment awaits them. These individuals are cursed and distance from divine mercy and guidance.
Lesson: No matter what hardship you are in never think bad or negative thoughts about Allah SWT!

translation.text: Surely those who pledge allegiance to you ˹O Prophet˺ are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. Allah’s Hand is over theirs. Whoever breaks their pledge, it will only be to their own loss. And whoever fulfils their pledge to Allah, He will grant them a great reward.

commentary.text: The pledge at Hudaibiyah was taken after rumors of Uthman's death in Makkah. Companions vowed not to retreat and to fight even unto death if required. This was basically a death sentence.

The allegiance sworn was to Allah SWT through His Messenger, with the Prophet’s (PBUH) hand acting as Allah’s representative. This is the honor given to the companions. So divine presence during the pledge. Pledge of Rizwan. Pledge of Allegiance is via Prophet to Allah SWT. Tripartite agreement.
Also see Surah Taubah Ayat 11. This exchange or barter between man (his life and wealth) and Allah SWT is the best barter.
Lesson: Anytime we are making a commitment for Allah SWT we are making a commitment to Allah SWT.

sections.title: 11-17 BEDUIN ARABS WHO DID NOT GO WITH THE PROPHET FOR WAR BETWEEN ISLAM AND KUFR ARE CONDEMNED FOR LAGGING BEHIND AND ONLY BLIND, LAME AND SICK ARE EXEMPT FROM WAR

translation.text: (O Prophet), the bedouins who were left behind say to you: “We were occupied with our goods and families. So ask forgiveness for us.” They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say to them: “Who can be of any avail to you against Allah if He should intend to cause you any harm or confer upon you any benefit?” Allah is well aware of all that you do.

commentary.text:
The Fabricated Excuse offered by Those Who lagged and did not participate in Al-Hلudaybiyyah; Allah SWT's Warning for Them
This refers to the people living in the suburbs of Al- Madinah whom the Prophet (PBUH) had invited to accompany for Umrah, but they had not left their homes in spite of their claim to faith just because they were afraid of death. But their hypocrisy is not hidden from Allah SWT.
Warning from Allah SWT: If Allah SWT intented any harm for them it would reach them no matter where they are.

Also, in Surah Muhammad the hypocrites expressed their desire for peace and no fighting. Now they thought that they Prophet and his followers would never come back from Umrah so they made excuses not to go.
Lesson: Devote yourself to Allah SWT and He will take care of you. What is the #1 reason that prevents you from striving in the way of Allah SWT? Home, money, job, children??

translation.text: When you [believers] set off for somewhere that promises war gains, those who [previously] stayed behind will say, ‘Let us come with you.’ They want to change God’s words, but tell them [Prophet], ‘You may not come with us: God has said this before.’ They will reply, ‘You begrudge us out of jealousy.’ How little they understand!

commentary.text: After the truce of Hudaibiyah, those who avoided earlier risks wanted to now join the Prophet (PBUH) when victory and rewards seemed likely/obvious as seen during the easy conquest of Khaiber which had fertile land and much war booty.
Allah SWT advised that only those who showed commitment at Hudaibiyah deserved these rewards; latecomers seeking easy gains would not be allowed to participate.
These people’s focus was the world and personal gain. Allah SWT promise is for those who work and strive only for Him.
FYI- These people would be allowed to take part in other future battles.

translation.text: Say to the bedouins who were left behind: “You will be called against those who possess great might and be asked to fight against them unless they surrender. If you obey (the command to fight), Allah will bestow upon you a goodly reward. But if you turn away, as you turned away before, He shall inflict upon you a grievous chastisement.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT directly addresses those who did not go. Next time if you are called then fulfill your duty and Allah SWT will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, i.e. `on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, when you were called to Jihad, yet lagged behind then He will punish you with a painful torment.

Lesson: Allah SWT will test you again and again. At times we lose the opportunity to do good and regret it. Next time no matter what grab on to the opportunity and be grateful to your Raab. Lip service is not enough rather striving and hard work is required.

translation.text: There is no blame on the blind, or the disabled, or the sick ˹for staying behind˺. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted by Him into Gardens under which rivers flow. But whoever turns away will be subjected by Him to a painful punishment.

commentary.text: Allah SWT now mentions the reasons that allow one to be excused from joining the Jihad.
Allah SWT clarifies that there is no blame on those who are genuinely unable to participate in jihad due to valid reasons such as blindness, disability, illness, or other legitimate constraints.

Islamic law recognizes real human limitations and does not impose duty where capacity is absent. What matters is not mere participation, but obedience and sincerity. Those who obey Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH) within their ability are promised Paradise, while those who deliberately turn away without excuse face punishment, in this world and the Hereafter.
Here, one should know that two kinds of the people have been exempted from jihad duty by the Shariah:

And whosoever obeys Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH), He will admit him to Gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whosoever turns back, (from joining the Jihad and busies himself in his livelihood) He will punish him with a painful torment, i.e. in this life with humiliation and in the Hereafter with the Fire.
In short: Islam excuses genuine incapacity but never excuses deliberate avoidance masked as necessity.

sections.title: 18-26 ALLAH WAS WELL PLEASED WITH THOSE SWORE ALLEGIANCE TO THE PROPHET BEFORE THE TREATY OF HUDEYBIYAH

translation.text: indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you ˹o prophet˺ under the tree. he knew what was in their hearts, so he sent down serenity upon them and rewarded them with a victory at hand,

commentary.text: Here again the pledge taken from the companions at Hudaibiyah has been mentioned. This is called Baiat Ridwan.
The Muslims at this time were equipped only with a sword each, numbered only 1,400, were unprepared for warfare.

Following the truce at Hudaibiyah, Allah SWT declared that only those who showed commitment by joining the Prophet (PBUH) there would be eligible for the rewards and spoils of Khaiber, excluding latecomers seeking easy gains.

Allah SWT further outlined legitimate exemptions from jihad, such as physical disability and other valid reasons, emphasizing that obedience to Allah and His Messenger leads to paradise, while turning away brings punishment.

Allah SWT expressed satisfaction with the believers who pledged allegiance under the tree, rewarding their sincerity with tranquility and imminent victory. Sakinat or serenity means that state of the heart on whose strength a man throws himself into dangers with complete calm and peace of mind regardless of the consequences.

Lesson: Total reliance on Allah SWT and then Allah SWT will help as well via victories/Sakina etc etc. Seek serenity from Allah SWT esp in times of stress and in sha Allah, Allah SWT will send it your way.

translation.text: Allah has promised you abundant spoils which you shall acquire. He has instantly granted you this (victory) and has restrained the hands of people from you that it may be a Sign for the believers and He may guide you to a Straight Way.

commentary.text: Allah SWT reassures the believers that the apparent restraint at Ḥudaybiyyah was not loss but strategy. He promises abundant future spoils, which came three months after the treaty i.e the victorty of Khaybar, and declares that the Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah itself was an immediate victory.
Allah SWT also reminds them that He restrained the enemies’ hands, preventing Quraysh from attacking at a moment when the Muslims were militarily vulnerable.

translation.text: And ˹there are˺ other gains which are beyond your reach that Allah is keeping in store ˹for you˺. For Allah is Most Capable of everything.

commentary.text: THIS IS A SURAH OF GOOD NEWS. AFTER HUDABIYA HISTORY CHANGED FOR THE MUSLIMS. VICTORY AFTER VICTORY!

translation.text: They are the ones who persisted in disbelief and hindered you from the Sacred Mosque, preventing the sacrificial animals from reaching their destination. ˹We would have let you march through Mecca,˺ had there not been believing men and women, unknown to you. You might have trampled them underfoot, incurring guilt for ˹what you did to˺ them unknowingly. That was so Allah may admit into His mercy whoever He wills. Had those ˹unknown˺ believers stood apart, We would have certainly inflicted a painful punishment on the disbelievers.

commentary.text: This was the reason why Allah SWT did not allow fighting to take place at Hudaibiyah.

(i) At that time there were many Muslims living in Makkah, who were either hiding their faith, or were being persecuted because of their faith as they had no means to emigrate. Had there been fighting these Muslims could also have been killed in ignorance along with the disbelievers.

(ii) Allah SWT did not will that Makkah should fall to the Muslims because of the defeat of the Quraish after a bloody clash rather He willed that they (Quraish) should become absolutely helpless and subdued accept defeat without offering any resistance, as it happened on the conquest of Makkah -- just two years later.
Lesson: Allah SWT knows the MACRO while we focus on the MICRO. So, trust in Allah’s Plan.

translation.text: ˹Remember˺ when the disbelievers had filled their hearts with pride—the pride of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance—then Allah sent down His serenity upon His Messenger and the believers, inspiring them to uphold the declaration of faith, for they were better entitled and more worthy of it. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

commentary.text: Pride and Arrogance is a trait the Allah SWT does not like. Allah SWT tells His believers how to act that is with taqwa, humility and sabr.
WHOEVER LOWERS HIMSELF FOR ALLAH SWT THEN ALLAH SWT ELEVATES HIM.

sections.title: 27-29 VISION TO CONQUER MAKKAH IS SHOWN TO THE HOLY PROPHET AND CHARACTERISTICS OF MUHAMMAD (PBUH) AND HIS FOLLOWERS

translation.text: Indeed, Allah will fulfil His Messenger’s vision in all truth: Allah willing, you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, in security—˹some with˺ heads shaved and ˹others with˺ hair shortened—without fear. He knew what you did not know, so He first granted you the triumph at hand.

commentary.text: Allah SWT fulfilled the dream of the Prophet (PBUH) of performing Umrah, clarifying that the delay was due to Divine Will, not opposition. Ultimately, Umrah was performed the following year in Dhil-Qadah A.H.7, known as Umrah al-Qada (delayed).
Allah SWT says you just wanted Umrah while Allah SWT wanted much more!
Lesson: Many times, we aim low while Allah SWT wants much more for us! Treaty was part of Allah SWT’s plan to spread Islam far and wide. It made others recognize Islam as a religion.

translation.text: He is the One Who has sent His Messenger with ˹right˺ guidance and the religion of truth, making it prevail over all others. And sufficient is Allah as a Witness.

commentary.text: When the Hudaibiyah Peace Treaty was going to be written down, the disbelievers had objected to the use of the words Rasul-Allah (Messenger of Allah) with the name of the Prophet (PBUH), and on their insistence the Prophet (PBUH) himself had removed these words from the document.

At this Allah SWT says: Our Messenger’s being a Messenger is a reality which remains unaffected whether someone believes in it or not. Their denial will not change the reality, but the guidance and the true faith which this Messenger (PBUH) has brought from Us, shall prevail over all religion, no matter how hard the deniers try to obstruct its progress.
Here what Allah SWT has stated in clear words is: The purpose of the Prophet’s (PBUH) appointment as a Prophet was not merely to preach this religion but to make it prevail over all others.

You see them bowing and prostrating ˹in prayer˺, seeking Allah’s bounty and pleasure. The sign ˹of brightness can be seen˺ on their faces from the trace of prostrating ˹in prayer˺. This is their description in the Torah. And their parable in the Gospel is that of a seed that sprouts its ˹tiny˺ branches, making it strong. Traits of the Companions of the Prophet (PBUH):
In their dealings with disbelievers, they are strong, firm and unyielding/unintimidated towards falsehood.

front_matter.text: This Surah was revealed during the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)'s final years in Madinah.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
This Surah is also called the SURAH OF MANNERS because it instructs Muslims on proper conduct esp. regarding Allah SWT and His Prophet (PBUH). This is almost like a parting gift from Allah SWT to his Messenger (PBUH). Good conduct is rooted in mercy and compassion and does not allow mocking or making fun of others.
It addresses how Muslims should respond if two groups fight and urges the community to avoid behaviors like mocking, prying, and backbiting, which harm relationships and society.
The Surah condemns prejudice based on nationality or ancestry, emphasizing that all humans descend from one pair and distinctions exist only for recognition, not for superiority. It concludes that genuine faith is shown through sincere belief, obedience, and striving in Allah’s SWT’s cause; mere verbal profession without heartfelt commitment does not make one a true believer in the eyes of Allah SWT.

sections.title: 1-10 ALLAH'S COMMANDMENT TO LOWER THE VOICE IN THE PRESENCE OF HOLY PROPHET AND MAKE PEACE BETWEEN THE BELIEVERS IF THEY FELL INTO FIGHTING AMONG THEMSELVES

arabic_lines: يٰۤاَيُّهَا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا لَا تُقَدِّمُوۡا بَيۡنَ يَدَىِ اللّٰهِ وَرَسُوۡلِهٖ وَ اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَؕ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ سَمِيۡعٌ عَلِيۡمٌ

translation.text: O believers! Do not proceed ˹in any matter˺ before ˹a decree from˺ Allah and His Messenger. And fear Allah. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

commentary.text: The first command is that true believers should never place their own opinions above the decisions of Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH). Instead, they are instructed/commanded to follow rather than lead, seeking guidance on all matters and remaining subordinate to divine instruction.

When a command comes then accept, for example, 4 fard rakats for zuhur salah means 4!, and one cannot in the guise of being extra pious make it 6 rakats. SO DO NOT INNOVATE OR LEGISLATE IN RELIGION!!!
Similarly, do not ignore commandments either, for example, missing salah as this is the essence of Kufur/denial.
Islam means to submit and surrender to Allah SWT. A believer is humble and submissive.

If ever you adopted an attitude of independence as against Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH), or gave priority to your own opinion and view over His command, you should know that you must deal with Alah SWT Who is All Hearing and All Knowing and is even aware of your secret intentions.

Pakistan’s constitution states no legislation can be done that is repugnant to the Quran and sunnah. Legislative authority is limited by the injunctions of the Quran and Sunnah. Then within that limit or circle one can make laws for example, at a dinner people discuss what drink to serve i.e., Pepsi or water etc., but alcohol is not an option.
Lesson: We cannot add or subtract anything from Iman/Deen. Dua: Allah SWT make me love what you love.
NOW NEXT 4 AYATS ARE REGARDING THE PROPHET AND HOW TO SHOW RESPECT TOWARDS HIM.

translation.text: O believers! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you do to one another, or your deeds will become void while you are unaware.

commentary.text: Reason: The immediate occasion involved Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, who raised their voices while disagreeing in the Prophet’s presence about leadership among Banū Tamīm. Though they were the best of the Companions, Allah SWT still corrected them to establish an absolute standard of reverence for the Prophet (PBUH). After the revelation, ʿUmar lowered his voice so much that the Prophet (PBUH) sometimes had to ask him to repeat himself.

This etiquette was taught to those meeting the Prophet (PBUH) to ensure they addressed him with utmost respect, never raising their voices above his or speaking to him with an unnecessary informality thus, recognizing his unique status.  This is part of our faith. 

This etiquette is for all people and all times. Everyone should observe the same respect and reverence when the Prophet (PBUH)’s name is mentioned, or a command of his is stated, or his sayings are explained.
Besides, this Ayat also points out what attitude the people should adopt when talking to persons of a higher rank and status than themselves whether it be parents, teachers etc.
The Prophet (PBUH) holds a uniquely high status in Islam, and any disrespect toward him is considered as very serious! So never just say his name without (PBUH) his full title of Rasool of Allah SWT.
Lesson: Be careful because this unintentional disrespect can cause deeds to be nullified.

translation.text: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of Allah’s Messenger are the ones whose hearts Allah has refined for righteousness. They will have forgiveness and a great reward.

commentary.text: Those who give due reverence and show respect to the Messenger (PBUH) of Allah, have passed successfully through the tests and trials set by Allah SWT and proved by their steadfastness that their hearts indeed possess taqwa (piety). Our actions show how much piety we have in our hearts.
Lesson: Generally, don’t be loud or raise your voice. The Prophet (PBUH) never laughed loudly although he smiled often.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ الَّذِيۡنَ يُنَادُوۡنَكَ مِنۡ وَّرَآءِ الۡحُجُرٰتِ اَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُوۡنَ

translation.text: Indeed, most of those who call out to you ˹O Prophet˺ from outside ˹your˺ private quarters have no understanding ˹of manners˺.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed about A delegation of the Banu Tamim who went to see the Prophet (PBUH). They entered the mosque and called the Prophet (PBUH) who was in his private apartment: 'O Muhammad, come out to meet us..”

Hujjarat or private quarters of the Prophet (PBUH) is being mentioned here. Allah SWT admonished those who called the Prophet (PBUH) from outside his private dwellings. These beduinons were unaware of the proper etiquette of addressing the Prophet and the sanctity of his private space.
This Ayat emphasizes the importance and understanding of personal boundaries. It is a call to embody thoughtfulness and wisdom in our actions.
Lesson: Reflect on the decorum and respect you give to people of leadership or guidance. How do we approach them? Are we aware of boundaries and manners in our interactions?

translation.text: Had they been patient until you could come out to them, it would have certainly been better for them. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: During the Prophet's (PBUH) time, those trained in Islamic etiquette respected his schedule and waited for appropriate times to visit, only seeking him when necessary.

However, visitors from distant areas often lacked these manners, sometimes shouting outside his home to get his attention, causing him distress despite his patience. Eventually, Allah SWT instructed people to wait quietly for the Prophet (PBUH) rather than disturb him.
This was more due to ignorance than arrogance therefore Allah SWT says he is Most forgiving and Most Merciful.
Lesson: Be respectful of others time and space.
NOW 8 AYATS TO MAKE THE ISLAMIC STATE STRONG AND UNITED.

translation.text: Believers, if a troublemaker brings you news, check it first, in case you wrong others unwittingly and later regret what you have done,

commentary.text: Reason: Many commentators state that this Ayat was revealed about Walid bin Uqbah bin Abi Muait. After being sent to collect Zakat from the Bani al-Mustaliq tribe, Walid returned to Al-Madinah claiming they refused to pay and threatened him. The Prophet (PBUH) considered sending a punitive expedition, but before action was taken, the tribe's chief, Harith bin Dirar, arrived with a delegation to clarify they had not seen Walid and had no intention of withholding Zakat. As a result, this Ayat was sent down.

Now another important command is being given. Upon receiving important news about significant matters, one should not accept it immediately but first assess the credibility of the source. If the informant is known to be unreliable or immoral, further investigation/clarity is required before acting on the information.

This principle underpins various Islamic legal practices, such as the authentication of hadiths and the use of evidence in Shariah law, where testimony from untrustworthy individuals is not accepted for consequential matters. However, this scrutiny is not necessary for trivial, everyday news, and evidence from those considered unrighteous due to incorrect beliefs (but not lying) is still acceptable.

Lesson: (i) Understand people’s intentions/character. (ii) Before forming an opinion investigate (iii) Do not pass on everything you have heard (iv) where there is ambiguity seek clarification, for example, when the Prophet (PBUH) saw a man come out of one of his wives’ quarters he inquired and found that was her brother (v) assume good of others.

translation.text: And keep in mind that Allah’s Messenger is ˹still˺ in your midst. If he were to yield to you in many matters, you would surely suffer ˹the consequences˺. But Allah has endeared faith to you, making it appealing in your hearts. And He has made disbelief, rebelliousness, and disobedience detestable to you. Those are the ones rightly guided.
˹This is˺ a bounty and a blessing from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

commentary.text: Core message here is to follow the Prophet (PBUH) because he is Allah SWT’s Messenger -- instead of following our own whims and desires.
For believers faith/Iman is very appealing and fills hearts with peace and contentment whereas any kind of sin makes a believer uncomfortable and detestable. This is a gift from Allah SWT.

translation.text: If two parties of the believers happen to fight, make peace between them. But then, if one of them transgresses against the other, fight the one that transgresses until it reverts to Allah’s command. And if it does revert, make peace between them with justice, and be equitable for Allah loves the equitable.

commentary.text: When a serious conflict arises among believers then make peace among them. This is a divine command to restore peace and fairness and harmony. If one transgresses over the other, then action must be taken. Confront oppressors until they return to what is good and right.
Allah SWT loves those who are just and equitable in all aspects of life.
Lesson: This command is mostly for those in authority and not a casual bystander.

translation.text: The Believers are but a single Brotherhood: So make peace and reconciliation between your two (contending) brothers; and fear Allah, that ye may receive Mercy.

commentary.text: All believers are related to one another via Iman.
One of the best charities is to make peace/amends between people.

sections.title: 11-13 ISLAMIC ETIQUETTES OF MORAL BEHAVIOR

translation.text: O you who have believed, let not a people (i) ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not (ii) insult one another and do not call each other by (iii) [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one''s] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.

commentary.text: In the preceding two Ayats the believers were made to realize that by virtue of their faith they are brothers to one another, and they should fear Allah SWT and try to keep their mutual relations right.

Now, in the following two Ayats believers are being enjoined to avoid and reject major evils which generally spoil the mutual relationships. Ridiculing/mocking, Slandering; taunting; harboring suspicions and spying on others are, in fact, the evils that cause mutual enmities and then lead to grave mischief. Allah SWT says it could be the person you are making fun of is better than you – don’t look down on people with arrogance and pride.

Women are being addressed separately here because women tend to do this more. That is, women should not make fun of other women. In a group setting people but especially women tent to get relaxed and start talking/gossiping. A typical conversation of women usually revolves around other people.

Do not ridicule or mock others. Ridicule or mocking does not only imply mocking with the tongue, but it also includes mimicking somebody, making pointed references to him, laughing at his words, or his works, or his appearance, or his dress, or calling the people’s attention to some defect or blemish in him so that others also may laugh at him. What is forbidden is that one should make fun of and ridicule another, for under such ridiculing there always lie feelings of one’s own superiority and the other’s abasement and contempt. Both men and women are addressed as no one is exempt from this prohibition. That person being ridiculed may be better in the sight of Allah SWT.
Do not insult or defame one another by words or actions.

Do not call each other with offensive nicknames. This command requires that a person should not be called by a name or a title which may cause him humiliation, e.g. calling somebody a sinner or a hypocrite, or calling someone a lame or blind one, or one-eyed etc. Only those nicknames have been made an exception from this command which serve as a mark of recognition or given out of love, like Abu Hurairah (father of the kitten) and Abu Turab (father of the dust).
We should focus on increasing our faith/Iman and not only these things.
There is a call for repentance against these wrong actions.
Lesson: Respect, dignity and maintaining harmonious relations are core ethical concepts in Islam.
THE ABOVE THREE THINGS ARE APPARENT AND NOW THE NEXT THREE THINGS MENTIONED IN AYAT 12 ARE HIDDEN.

translation.text: Believers, avoid making too many assumptions– some assumptions are sinful– and do not spy on one another or speak ill of people behind their backs: would any of you like to eat the flesh of your dead brother? No, you would hate it. So be mindful of God: God is ever relenting, most merciful.

commentary.text: THESE ARE THREE THINGS THAT ALLAH SWT HAS STOPPED US FROM.

Avoid making too many conjecture/assumptions. Assuming the intent of another person is not inherently wrong. The guidance is not to avoid all suspicion, but to avoid excessive suspicion as it can lead to misunderstandings for example, silence does not mean you are upset it can mean you are enjoying some me time. Overthinking leads to problems like analyzing every conversation etc.

Do not spy on one another. Spying, or enquiring too curiously into other people's affairs, means either idle curiosity, or seeking out others faults often with ill intention which undermines trust and community harmony. Don’t look at others phones, private diaries, etc.
Hadith: Those who search for other people’s faults will be humiliated in their own houses.

Back-biting is strongly condemned and likened to the eating of a dead brother’s flesh. Backbiting is like that because the person is not there to defend itself like a dead body where you can take a bite from whenever. This is how abhorrent a sin it is.
Hadith: Backbiting is talking about someone in their absence in a way they dislike whether it is true or false. If it is true, it is backbiting and if it is false, it is slander.
Allah SWT’s Mercy is emphasized because despite human short comings Allah SWT is always ready to accept sincere repentance.
Lesson: Always assume the best as negative assumptions lead to mistrust and corrupt feelings.

translation.text: O humanity! Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may ˹get to˺ know one another. Surely the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous among you. Allah is truly All-Knowing, All-Aware.

commentary.text: In the preceding Ayats Muslims are given necessary instructions to safeguard the community against social evils.

In this Ayat all mankind is addressed to reform it of the great evil that has always been causing universal disruption in the world, that is, the prejudices due to race, color, language, country, and nationality.

On account of these prejudices man drawing around himself some small circles and regarding those born within those circles as his own people and those outside them as others. These circles have been drawn on the basis of accidental birth and not on rational and moral grounds.
This discrimination can often assume the worst forms of hatred, enmity, contempt and tyranny.

In this Ayat, Allah SWT has drawn the attention of all mankind to three cardinal truths: 
(1) The origin of all of you is one and the same. Your whole species has sprung up from one man and one woman.
(2) In spite of being one in origin, it was natural that you should be divided into nations and tribes. 
(3) The only basis of superiority and excellence that there is, or can be, between man and man is that of moral excellence (TAQWA). As regards birth, all men are equal, for their Creator is One, their substance of creation is one, and their way of creation is one, and they are descended from the same parents.

The real thing that makes one person superior to others is that one should be more God-conscious (TAQWA), one who avoids evils, and a follower of the way of piety and righteousness. 

In this connection, a misunderstanding also needs to be removed. In the case of marriage, the importance that Islamic law gives to kufv (likeness of status) has been taken by some people in the sense that some brotherhoods are noble and some mean, and matrimonial relations between them are objectionable.

But this, in fact, is a wrong idea. According to the Islamic law, every Muslim man can marry every Muslim woman, but the success of the matrimonial life depends on maximum harmony and conformity between the spouses as regards habits, characteristics and ways of life, family traditions and economic and social status, so that they may get on well with each other. This is the real object of being equal and alike.

Where there is unusual difference and disparity between the man and the woman in this regard, lifelong companionship will be difficult. That is why the Islamic law disapproves of such intermarriages, and not for the reason that one of the spouses is noble and the other mean, but for the reason that in case there is a clear and apparent difference and distinction in status, there would be a greater possibility of the failure of the matrimonial life if the marriage relationship was established.

commentary.text: Allah SWT chastises the Bedouins who, when they embraced Islam, claimed for themselves the grade of faithful believers. However, Iman had not yet firmly entered their hearts.

This Ayat provides proof that Faith/Iman is a higher grade than Islam, this is also demonstrated in the Hadith of Angel Jibril when he questioned the Prophet (PBUH) about Islam, then Iman then Ihsan. 
Keep in mind that the Bedouins whom the Ayat mentioned were not hypocrites, rather they were Muslims in whose hearts Faith was not yet firmly established.
Iman is internal and Muslim is outward in conduct. This world outward laws are all according to Islam, yet Iman is for the Hereafter.

translation.text: The ˹true˺ believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger—never doubting—and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. They are the ones true in faith.

commentary.text: True definition of a Momin: Absolute/Total/Firm belief in Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH) that is inward (in the heart) and then striving with their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah SWT. So, five pillars of Islam (Muslim)+ the two traits mentioned above (striving with their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah SWT) = Momin.
This is the only place in the Quran where Iman and Islam is separated.
FYI – Hypocrites are not being mentioned here rather just plain Muslims.
Assess how much time and energy is focused on this world compared to the jihad for Allah SWT. Momin and sadiqeen should be our ideal. Reach out to that community and attach yourself to them.
Def of Iman = 7 qualities.
