front_matter.text: The Surah’s name is from the initial letter Qaf.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Its period of revelation is the second stage of the Holy Prophet's life at Makkah, which lasted from the third year of the Prophethood till the fifth year.

front_matter.label: Theme and Topics
front_matter.text:
The Surah's main theme is the Hereafter, addressing people's initial disbelief in resurrection after death. It provides brief arguments supporting the possibility of life after death and asserts that Allah SWT has complete knowledge and power to resurrect every individual.
The Surah warns that everyone is accountable for their actions, (which are recorded by angels), and will ultimately be rewarded or punished in the afterlife according to their deeds.
Last surahs are short have a rhythmic and flow divine music. In Arabic, the word "Intezar" (انتظار) means anticipation, expectation, or waiting. It carries the meaning of patience and hope for a better future or a longed-for event, and when used in a religious context, it can refer to awaiting Divine blessings, or the coming of relief.
These are from the first 4 years of Prophethood in Mecca. First command was intezar in tableeqh. Life has a purpose more than just eating and sleeping everything is for a finite period. Then accountability on DoJ. This is intezar. Those who don’t fear DoJ don’t understand.
Barkat means that take the potential good out of something or bring it to surface. Like rain brings the earth of life with food and beauty.

sections.title: 1-15 LIFE AFTER DEATH IS A REALITY AND THERE IS NOTHING STRANGE ABOUT IT

translation.text: Qãf. By the glorious Quran!
Will we be returned to life, when we are dead and reduced to dust? Such a return is impossible.

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the Glorious/Honorable Quran that we will all be resurrected.

translation.text: ˹All will be resurrected,˺ yet the deniers are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves ˹warning of resurrection˺. So the disbelievers say, “This is an astonishing thing!

commentary.text: The disbelievers said, after we die, disintegrate, with our organs torn apart and we become dust, how can we be brought back to our original shape and bodies, that such a thing never happen.

However, they could not agree upon a single allegation or assertion calling the Prophet (PBUH) a madman, a poet, a magician etc. Their contradictory accusations reflected their confusion and denial of the truth. Therefore, the Quran proceeds to present clear reasoning about the reality of the Hereafter, which they considered impossible.

translation.text: In fact, they reject the truth when it has come to them, so they are in a confused state.

commentary.text: Deniers are always in a state of confusion and uncertainty. Without Iman there is superstition and no confidence. But with Iman there is a foundation, clarity and certainty but we have to have faith in the unseen.

translation.text: As for the earth, We spread it out and placed upon it firm mountains, and produced in it every type of pleasant plant

commentary.text: How can we deny when we look at the towering mountains, and every kind of plant.

translation.text: ˹all as˺ an insight and a reminder to every servant who turns ˹to Allah˺.

commentary.text: Creation is not in vain rather it is enough to open someone’s eyes. We have reminders and Allah SWT’s Ayats all around us.

translation.text: And We send down blessed rain from the sky, bringing forth gardens and grains for harvest,

commentary.text: Allah SWT has sent down water/rain to bring vegetation and gardens back to life again and again.

translation.text: and towering palm trees ˹loaded˺ with clustered fruit,
all this as sustenance for Our servants. And thus We do bring the dead land back to life with water. Such shall be the coming forth (of human beings from the earth).

commentary.text: All this provision is a reminder for us to understand and appreciate our Raab. If Allah SWT can revive plants, then He is fully capable of resurrecting us after we are in our graves. Allah SWT will send a special rain, and dead bodies will come out of their graves just like plants sprout out of the earth with rain.
Yet the people of the past, including the nations of Nuh, Lut, Hud, Ad, Thamud all denied.

translation.text: So were We incapable of the first creation? No indeed! Yet they doubt a second creation.

commentary.text: These are all arguments for the Hereafter. Man cannot deny the excellently ordered universe and the creation of man is not a mere accident and must admit that Allah SWT alone has created man and this whole universe.

Had God been powerless, He would not have been able to create all this in the first instance. When He has created the universe in the first instance and mankind came into existence by virtue of that act of creation, what can then be the rational ground for assuming that He will become powerless to re-make the dismantled thing originally made by Himself?

sections.title: 16-29 ALLAH HAS ASSIGNED TWO ANGELS TO EACH PERSON FOR NOTING DOWN EACH SINGLE WORD THAT HE UTTERS

translation.text: Indeed, ˹it is˺ We ˹Who˺ created humankind and ˹fully˺ know what their souls whisper to them, and We are closer to them than ˹their˺ jugular vein.

commentary.text: After presenting the arguments for the Hereafter, it is being stated: Whether you believe in the Hereafter, or deny it, it is a reality which will certainly happen/come.
Allah SWT’s Power and Knowledge encompasses man so much so that Allah SWT is closer to him than his own jugular-vein. Allah SWT directly know every thought that arises in his heart.

Lesson: This is a matter of the unseen so we should accept that indeed Allah SWT is very close to us. Similarly, when He comes down at time of night prayers are matters of the unseen, but belief here is essential.

translation.text: Moreover, there are two scribes, one each sitting on the right and the left, recording everything.

commentary.text: in reference to the two angels who receive and record the deeds of mankind.
One sitting on the right (good deeds) and one on the left (bad deeds).
Hadith: Our angel on the left holds back his pen for six hours because if we repent then that sin will not be written down. So, when we commit a sin we have a window of repentance. USE IT!

translation.text: not a word does a person utter without having a ˹vigilant˺ observer ready ˹to write it down˺.

commentary.text: On the one hand, Allah SWT knows man’s actions and movements, even his hidden thoughts; on the other hand, every man has two angels appointed over him, who are recording whatever he does and says, none of his actions or words is left unrecorded.
Man’s own body and limbs will testify for or against him. Thus, a complete, unbiased, clear proof with undeniable evidence becomes available of everyone’s life work and activity.
Thus, when man is produced in the court of Allah, Allah SWT then every human will know exactly where he stands and there will be evidence to prove it.

arabic_lines: وَجَآءَتْ   سَكْرَةُ   ٱلْمَوْتِ   بِٱلْحَقِّ   ۖ   ذَٰلِكَ   مَا   كُنتَ   مِنْهُ   تَحِيدُ

translation.text: Lo, the agony of death has indeed come with the Truth. That is what you had sought to avoid.

commentary.text: The agony/pangs/stupor/pain of death (Sukarat ul Mut) is the starting point when the reality which had remained concealed in the world, is finally unveiled.  Man’s limbs/body and mind are not functioning as they are supposed to. At this point man starts seeing clearly the other world of which the Prophet (PBUH) had forewarned him. Here, man knows whether he is entering this second stage of life as favored or damned.
Man, desires that he should live this life as if there is no consequence of another life and avoids thinking about death.
Lesson: If we are going on a trip or to a wedding, we prepare so how much are we preparing for death? How often do we think of death. We cannot afford to be headless of this Day.
Unbelievers don’t think about this Day because they think they can escape it but they know they can’t escape death.

translation.text: And the Trumpet will be blown. This is the Day ˹you were˺ warned of.
Everyone has come, each attended by one who will drive him on, and another who will bear witness.

commentary.text: On the Day of Resurrection, when every man will rise from his grave on the sounding of the Trumpet, the two angels will come forth immediately and take him into their custody. One of them will drive him to the divine court and the other will be carrying his record.

arabic_lines: لَقَدۡ كُنۡتَ فِىۡ غَفۡلَةٍ مِّنۡ هٰذَا فَكَشَفۡنَا عَنۡكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الۡيَوۡمَ حَدِيۡدٌ

commentary.text: After death the veil will be removed and finally, we will see things clearly and as they are. For the first time we will understand the reality that Allah SWT via His Prophets (PBU Them) have been telling us.
Presently we live life as if we are sleeping, that is, in heedlessness.

Everyone who hindered good, was aggressive, caused others to doubt,
who set up another god with Allah. So cast them into the severe punishment.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT, in these Ayat, has enumerated the qualities that make a man worthy of Hell: (i) Every Stubborn, Persistent Disbeliever (ii) One who stops others from good and he himself is uncertain and then casts doubts/confusion in people’s minds/hearts (iii) Commits Shrik.

sections.title: 30-35 HELL SHALL BE ASKED, "ARE YOU FULL" HELL WILL ANSWER, "ARE THERE ANY MORE?"

translation.text: On that Day We shall ask Hell: “Are you full?” And it will reply: “Are there anymore?”

commentary.text: The people will be thrown into Jahannam (Hell) and it (hell) will say, `Are there anymore?' Meaning there is still room for more people.
Lesson: Hell is an entity that is to be feared. It is not just a place in our imagination rather a thriving entity.

translation.text: And when Paradise shall be brought close to the God-fearing, and will no longer be far away,

commentary.text: As soon as the judgment is passed about a person from the court of Allah SWT that he is righteous and worthy of Paradise, he will immediately find Paradise in front of him. He will not have to travel a distance on foot or by a conveyance to reach to it. There will be no interval between the pronouncement of the judgment and his entry into the Paradise. From this it can be judged how different the concept of space and time is between this world and the Hereafter.
Paradise is for those who have TAQWA.

translation.text: ˹And it will be said to them,˺ “This is what you were promised, for whoever ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺ and kept up ˹His commandments˺—

commentary.text: This is the promise of Allah SWT for the ones who constantly repent (because man sins often) and turn back to Allah SWT in mindfulness and with Iman. Someone who is alter and mindful of Allah SWT rights upon man.

arabic_lines: مَّنْ   خَشِىَ   ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ   بِٱلْغَيْبِ   وَجَآءَ   بِقَلْبٍ   مُّنِيبٍ

translation.text: who were in awe of the Most Compassionate without seeing ˹Him˺ and have come with a heart turning ˹only to Him˺.

commentary.text: The believer fears Allah SWT even though he cannot see Him. His fear is not based on visible power or worldly authority, but on faith in the unseen. Even though he knows Allah SWT is Most Merciful, he does not use that mercy as an excuse to sin. Instead, he remains careful about his words and actions, fearing Allah’s displeasure.

The Ayat uses khashiyyah, not khauf. This means the believer’s fear is not just about punishment. It comes from recognizing Allah SWT majesty and grandeur. That sense of awe keeps the believer spiritually alert at all times.
Khauf: fear caused by weakness in front of power.
Khashiyyah: awe and reverence caused by greatness and majesty.

translation.text: Enter it in peace. This is the Day of eternal life!”

commentary.text: May we all be of the ones that hear these amazing words!! Ameen Summa Ameen. This is the beginning of eternity.

Criteria for Paradise mentioned here is: (i) Taqwa, (ii) Repentance and turning back to Allah SWT (iii) Following/Obeying His Commands (iv) the one who fears Allah SWT based on his faith of the unseen.

commentary.text: The residents of Paradise will certainly get whatever they desire, but in addition We will also give them that which they have never conceived and, therefore, could not desire.

commentary.text: There were two ordained prayers prior to the Isra' journey. One before the rising of the sun at dawn and the other before sunset in the evening. Qiyam Al-Layl, prayer at night, was a command for the Prophet (PBUH) and his followers for some time but it was later abrogated for the Ummah. Later, during the Isra' journey, Allah SWT abrogated all of the previous orders for prayer by ordaining five daily prayers, including the prayers of Fajr before sunrise, and `Asr in the late afternoon.

front_matter.text: سۡمِ اللهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِ

front_matter.label: JUZ
front_matter.text: JUZ 26

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name of this Surah is from the very first word wadh-dhariyat of Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This Surah also seems to have been revealed in the same period in which the Surah Qaf was revealed.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
Surah Adh-Dhariyat is called the SURAH OF PROVISION because lets us know that our رزق is already assigned by Allah SWT.
The winds that scatter clouds, the rain that revives dead land, the earth that produces food, the skies that hold your provision. All of it is controlled, measured, and delivered with precision. No chaos. No freelancing atoms.
Our purpose is worship.
Our provision is guaranteed.
Our accountability is inevitable.
That’s why it’s called the Surah of Provision. Not because it promises wealth, but because it teaches trust.
The Surah too mostly deals with the Hereafter, and in the end, it presents the invitation to Tauhid. In addition, the people have also been warned that refusal to accept the message of the Prophets and persistence in the concepts and creeds of ignorance have proved to be disastrous for those nations themselves which have adopted this attitude and way of life in the past.
This Surah highlights that differing beliefs about the Hereafter are based on speculation rather than knowledge. Relying on conjecture for such a crucial issue is risky, as it can misguide a person’s life and leave them unprepared for what follows death.
The proper approach is to reflect on the Prophet (PBUH)'s teachings about the Hereafter and study the world and human existence for supporting evidence. The wind, rain, earth’s structure, paired creation, and historical examples are presented as proof of the necessity for retribution in the universe.
The text explains that humans were created to serve their Creator. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is advised to continue his mission for the benefit of believers, regardless of resistance, as those who persist in rebellion will eventually face consequences just as previous generations did.

sections.title: 1-23 SURELY THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT SHALL COME TO PASS, ONLY THE PERVERSE PERSONS TURN AWAY FROM THIS TRUTH

translation.text: By the winds which scatter dust,
and ˹the clouds˺ loaded with rain,
and ˹the ships˺ gliding with ease,
and ˹the angels˺ administering affairs by ˹Allah’s˺ command!
Indeed, what you are promised is true.

commentary.text: Whatever we have been promised about resurrection is true.

This Surah is also called the Surah of Provision because it reminds us that our sustenance is already decreed by Allah SWT, delivered through His perfectly ordered system, while our real responsibility is obedience. FYI – the winds, rain, ships, angels all provide sustenance for us.  How winds, rain, ships carrying heavy loads float on the seas, angels doing what they are instructed to do -- i.e. provide us with provision-- is all part of the unseen just like Resurrection. We cannot imagine where our provision might come from, but Allah SWT is the BEST PROVIDER. Our job is to have TAQWA and WORSHIP.

translation.text: and the Judgement shall doubtlessly take place.

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes oaths about the certainty of the Hereafter. The oaths were taken of the winds, the clouds filled with rain, ships and angels.

The perfect order of the universe, especially the precise system of rain, shows that this world is not random or meaningless. Everything runs with purpose and wisdom. So it makes no sense that human beings, who were given intellect, moral awareness, and free will, would be left unaccountable for how they lived.

Plants and animals fulfill their purpose in this world and end there. Humans, whose actions carry moral consequences, must face justice beyond death. And just as scattered water vapor is gathered again as rain, Allah SWT can easily reassemble scattered human bodies for resurrection. Accountability is not a mystery. It is the logical outcome of a purposeful creation.
FYI - It has the same style as other Surahs where Allah SWT takes an oath in the beginning.

translation.text: Doomed are the conjecturers

commentary.text: The Quran warns against building your entire worldview on guesswork when it comes to Allah SWT, accountability, and the Hereafter. Allah SWT sends guidance through His Prophets, and humans are meant to verify it by reflecting on the signs in creation, not by inventing theories, following personal assumptions thus choosing confusion over clarity.
Those who lie, fabricate and guess regarding Iman and Islam will be doomed.

translation.text: . those who are ˹steeped˺ in ignorance, totally heedless.

commentary.text: These people live under false assumptions about the Hereafter, unaware of where their beliefs are leading them. Some deny accountability altogether, others expect another chance after death, some hope for annihilation, and some rely on imagined intercessors. But when death arrives, all these illusions collapse. There is no return, no escape, no substitute for personal responsibility. Their beliefs are like a numbing drug, keeping them blind to reality while they walk steadily toward consequences they never prepared for.

translation.text: They ask ˹mockingly˺, “When is this Day of Judgment?”
On a Day when they will be punished by the Fire,

commentary.text: Disbelievers ask mockingly and without any seriousness about the DoJ so and then Allah SWT answers them in a fitting manner.

translation.text: ˹They will be told,˺ “Taste your torment! This is what you sought to hasten.”
As to the Righteous, they will be in the midst of Gardens and Springs,

commentary.text: On the other hand, below are the dwellers of Paradise and some of their qualities.

translation.text: they used to sleep but little by night,

commentary.text: Seldom did it so happen that they spent the whole night sleeping and did not spend a part of it, in the beginning of the night or in the middle or in the end of it, awake in the worship of Allah SWT

translation.text: and pray for forgiveness before dawn.

commentary.text: They did not belong to those who spent their nights in immoral and indecent acts still they sought Allah’s forgiveness. On the contrary, they spent a major part of the nights in the worship of Allah SWT and then in the early hours of dawn sought His forgiveness, saying that they did not do full justice to the worship that was due from them.
Lesson: Do istakfar in tahajud prayer esp. in sujood.

translation.text: And in their wealth there was a rightful share ˹fulfilled˺ for the beggar and the poor.

commentary.text: They recognized the right of their Lord and duly discharged it (prayer as mentioned above); and also they did not think that whatever Allah SWT had given them, whether little or much, was wholly their own and their children’s right, but they had the sense that in their possessions there was the right and share of every such person who was deprived/destitute and needy.

Here, one should also know and understand another thing; this does not imply zakat, which has been imposed as religious duty on them. In fact, the real spirit of this divine command is that a pious and virtuous person (even after paying zakat) remains ever ready to do whatever good he can do and does not let slip any opportunity when he could do some good to the people in the world.
لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَالۡمَحۡرُوۡم
Sa’il: the one who asks for help openly.
Mahrum: the one who is poor but does not ask.
The Mahrum may have no income, no profession, no support, and no visibility. They suffer quietly. The Prophet ﷺ made it clear: real poverty isn’t loud. It’s often invisible.

translation.text: And in heaven is your provision and also what you are being promised.

commentary.text: Allah SWT has already decided about each person’s provision, and it is written in the Heavens at the time of birth. All has been previously decreed and written in Loh Mahfooz.

Your sustenance doesn’t come from your job, your connections. It comes from Allah SWT. The sky is mentioned because rain, growth, and all life-sustaining systems are sent from above by His command. And the “promise” refers to the Hereafter, reward or accountability, already decreed and waiting.
Rizq is arranged.
Results are recorded.

Lesson: Don’t worry about jobs, provisions etc., as this is already decreed. Worry about obeying and worshipping Allah SWT to the best of our ability. Meaning don’t get caught up in life that is already decreed and fleeting.

translation.text: So, by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, this is certainly true, as true as the fact of your speaking.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is taking an oath that the Hereafter is true just like ur speaking.

sections.title: 24-30 STORY OF PROPHET IBRAHIM, WHEN HE WAS GIVEN A GOOD NEWS OF HAVING A SON

translation.text: Has the story of Abraham’s honoured guests reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

commentary.text: This story has been narrated at three places in the Quran, (i) Surah Hud Ayat 69-73 (ii) Surah Al Hijr Ayat 51-56 and Surah Al-Ankabut Ayat 31.
From here to the end of Ayat 46, brief allusions have been made, one after the other, about Allah SWT’s Prophets and some of the nations of the past, which are meant to impress two things:

First, that in human history God’s law of retribution has been working constantly, in which precedents are found of the rewards for the righteous and of punishments for the wicked people continuously.

The second thing that has been impressed by these historical allusions is that the nations which did not believe in the Prophets of Allah and based the conduct and attitude in life on the denial of the Oneness of Allah, the Prophethood and the Hereafter, were ultimately doomed to destruction.

translation.text: Then he slipped off to his family and brought a fat ˹roasted˺ calf,

commentary.text: Lesson: He served his guests with the best of what he had. Made arrangements in a subtle manner. Placed it before them. Not a lot of pushing them to eat or forcing them.

translation.text: Then he became afraid of them. They said: “Fear not,” and announced to him the good news of (the birth of) a boy endowed with knowledge.

commentary.text: When the guests did not stretch out their hands for food, then Prophet Abraham (PBUH) became afraid in his heart. The reason for this fear could be that in tribal life the strangers’ going to a house and avoiding food used to be an indication that they had come with an evil design. Prophet Abraham (PBUH) realized that they were angels, who had come in human guise; and since the angels came in human guise only on extraordinary occasions, he became afraid that they must have come on some dreadful mission.
Lesson: Hence the term “namak haram.” I presume. At least people had some decency those days as opposed to now when they eat and then rob.
They gave the goods news of the birth of Prophet Isaac (Ishaq) and Prophet Jacob (Yacub) (PBU Them).

Note: Allah SWT increases the risk or provision of those who give even when they barely have enough for themselves. Prophet Ibrahim served his guests, and Allah SWT gave him more risk via two amazing sons.
Prophet Musa defined himself as a beggar (in his dua to Allah SWT) yet he helped the girls. Allah SWT reared him with a house and wife.
SO EVEN WHEN WE HAVE NOTHING WE MUST KEEP GIVING!! AND KNOW THAT ALLAH SWT IS OUR PROVIDER.
And provision is provided in ways that we don’t understand or cannot even phantom as it is all part of Allah SWT’s plan and part of the unseen.
